mount-everest: The highest mountain on Earth, first climbed in 1953
k2: The second-highest mountain, the "Savage Mountain" on the Pakistan–China border
kangchenjunga: Third-highest, on the Nepal–Sikkim border; its name means "five treasures of snow"
lhotse: Fourth-highest, joined to the highest by the South Col
makalu: Fifth-highest, a sharp four-sided pyramid southeast of the highest peak
cho-oyu: Sixth-highest, often called the easiest 8,000-metre peak; name means "Turquoise Goddess"
manaslu: Eighth-highest, the "mountain of the spirit" in central Nepal
nanga-parbat: Ninth-highest, the western anchor of the Himalayas, nicknamed "Killer Mountain"
annapurna: Tenth-highest and historically the deadliest; the first 8,000er climbed (1950)
gasherbrum-i: Eleventh-highest, in the Karakoram, the higher of a numbered pair
broad-peak: Twelfth-highest, named for its long summit ridge, next to the second-highest mountain
gasherbrum-ii: Thirteenth-highest, a Karakoram peak often climbed with its higher twin
shishapangma: The lowest 8,000er and the only one entirely in Tibet
